analogs.covers: The whole daily life: the Galápagos lizard that grazes nothing but seaweed in the surf and shallows, sneezes the salt out through its nose, lies for hours in tight heaps on dark lava rock to soak up its warmth, lets small animals pick ticks and dead skin off its scales and only dives close to shore, never into the open sea

The temper and the float: a dominant bull who owns the water, bullfights between rivals, sun-sensitive skin and mud, fighting from the shallows, and the dry-season rage against anything that comes to the water's edge

headline: A marine iguana with a hippo's temper: grazes only kelp in the surf, snorts out salt, hides from the sun by day and warms up on sun-heated lava rock at night.

setting.label: Beaches, sea cliffs and islands
setting.note: Tallbrush Coasts, the Coastal Bluffs, the Volcano Islands and the Palm Islands. By day knee-deep in the surf and shallows, in the shade or in mud; small rock shelters right at the waterline only as a short refuge. At night out on the dark rocks that still hold the day's heat. Keeps close to shore; the open sea belongs to Tylosaurus. Processes salt water and needs no fresh water.

playsLike: You are the coastal Lurdusaurus, a medium semi-aquatic herbivore in a 'float' of up to 10 (max 5 males) on the beaches and islands. Your food is kelp and nothing else: you graze it in the surf and the shallows and snort the salt out of your nose in loud bursts. The sun is your problem: by day you stand knee-deep in the water, lie in the shade or coat yourself in mud, and you duck into a rock niche at the waterline only for a short while. After sunset the float climbs out onto the dark rock that soaked up the day's heat and lies there in a heap, while the bulls practise their bullfights. Males hold a stretch of coast against rival floats and other semi-aquatics. Up to 5 engage, bulls first, and you fight from the shallows. You flee Deinosuchus and Spinosaurus unless 5 adults are present, and you never swim out into deep water. In the dry season you attack anything, even Apexes, that approaches your water's edge.

why.text: "They have a unique ability to process salt water and utilise this to their advantage when in coastal regions - especially during the Dry Season. They expel salt through their nostrils in loud snorts." The marine iguana sneezes the salt from its nasal glands in exactly this way.

"Within the water they use their serrated beaks to graze on aquatic vegetation like lakeweed, kelp and reeds." Marine iguanas crop seaweed off the rocks in the surf and shallows; the coast variant keeps only the kelp.
They "can be seen gathered around clusters of these rocks from time to time" to lick salt. Marine iguanas lie together by the hundred on the same rocks.
Rhamphorhynchus are "rather perfect for clearing off stuck shed or water ticks clinging to their scales". Lava lizards, finches and crabs pick ticks and dead skin off marine iguanas.
"Lurdusaurus from coastal regions are known to have more blue, gray and white in their colors." The profile itself sets the coastal Lurdusaurus apart, and grey is the marine iguana's everyday colour.
"As the sun begins to set, they become far more lively, and willingly emerge from the water to travel a bit further inland." The coast variant spends that time on the warm rock.

The dominant bull and his subordinates hold a water territory, and in the dry season they aggress every species that approaches the water's edge, including Apexes. A marine iguana has no such temper; the hippo does.

notLike: The day is turned around. A marine iguana is cold-blooded and basks in the sun to warm up; the Lurdusaurus is "incredibly prone to overheating or even burning from the sun". So you shelter by day (shallows, shade, mud) and warm up on the sun-heated rock after dark. This is a reading of the profile, not a rule from it.
Kelp only is a choice for this variant. The profile also allows lakeweed, reeds, berries, shellfish, fruits and salt.
A rock shelter is a short refuge at the waterline, not a place to spend the day: the profile says they "almost exclusively prefer to remain in water" by day.
Marine iguanas are a metre long and harmless; you are Medium tier (3,200 combat weight, 600 HP), fight with thumb spikes and live in a float with a dominant bull.
twist: The coast half of the profile: an iguana that has to hide from the sun it would love, and gets its warmth from the lava at night instead. Your river cousin, the Schlammbader, plays the same profile as a hippo.
